novelty.justification: The claim proposes a new within-reasoning relationship: “the per-example gap between pivot-decodability and surface-decodability predicts whether the model will fail,” together with “Pivot Amplification” at reasoning-critical layers, so its novelty route is chiefly a finer-grained mechanism and measurement in multi-step reasoning rather than a new setting alone. Searches using “multilingual LLM internal English pivot language reasoning,” “language of thought decodability gap multilingual reasoning,” and “cross-lingual activation steering reasoning” identify the closest work as Wendler et al., “Do Multilingual LLMs Think In English?” (English-like intermediate representations and stronger English-derived steering), “Separating Tongue from Thought” (cross-language activation patching), and “Improving Multilingual Language Models by Aligning Representations through Steering”; these already establish the broad pivot-language and steering ideas. Moving to stepwise reasoning states, defining an example-level pivot-versus-surface decodability gap, and linking that gap to localized amplification is a substantive multi-step integration and natural extension of those results, but it does not require an entirely new core paradigm and partly renames standard contrastive activation steering for a reasoning-specific target.
